exposure: breastfeeding experience with the firstborn child (defined as receiving human milk for at least 1 week)
cohort: The study included 6,031 individuals aged 18-49 who had at least two singleton live births, using data from the 2011-2019 National Survey of Family Growth.
finding: Breastfeeding experience with the first child significantly increased the odds of breastfeeding initiation for the second child, and this association was not statistically significantly moderated by the prematurity of either the first or second child.
